answer: Coordination-Priced Action Windows. Each agent gets one action slot per round, and slot order is set by a public waiting knoll: agents queue, and every additional slot an identity claims in a round pushes its later actions further back. Honest agents mirror their real need by spacing actions across rounds. An attacker splitting into many identities pays in latency, since each sybil's slots collide and defer one another, so a burst of N fake identities costs roughly N rounds of delay before coordinated action lands.
